title: DP Volcano
description: Dynamic programming: solve each subproblem once and reuse the answer.

challenges.prompt: Count the ways to climb n stairs if you can take 1 or 2 steps at a time. What structure does the answer have?
challenges.explanation: Your last move was either 1 step (from n − 1) or 2 steps (from n − 2). It is the Fibonacci recurrence.

challenges.prompt: Solve climbing stairs bottom-up in O(1) space.
challenges.explanation: Only the last two answers are needed, so two variables replace the whole table. After the loop, b holds ways(n).

challenges.prompt: What is the time complexity of this naive recursion?
challenges.explanation: Each call spawns two more and the same values are recomputed again and again. Memoizing fib(k) brings it down to O(n).

challenges.prompt: Which two properties signal that a problem fits dynamic programming?
options: A graph and a start node
challenges.explanation: Overlapping subproblems means caching pays off; optimal substructure means the best answer is built from best answers to smaller pieces.

challenges.prompt: Coins are [1, 3, 4] and the amount is 6. Greedy always takes the biggest coin that fits. How many coins does greedy use, versus the optimum?
challenges.explanation: Greedy takes 4 + 1 + 1 = 3 coins, but 3 + 3 uses only 2. That is why coin change needs DP: dp[a] = 1 + min(dp[a − c]).

challenges.prompt: Find the longest common subsequence of two strings. What does the DP table look like?
options: 2D table: dp[i][j] for prefixes of both strings
A hash map of letter counts
challenges.explanation: If the characters match, dp[i][j] = dp[i−1][j−1] + 1; otherwise take the best of dropping a character from either string.

challenges.prompt: LCS of strings with lengths m and n fills every cell of the table once. Time complexity?
challenges.explanation: There are m × n cells and each takes O(1). Space can drop to O(min(m, n)) by keeping only two rows.

challenges.prompt: Pick items with weights and values to maximize total value without exceeding capacity W. Each item can be used once.
options: Sort by value and take greedily
0/1 knapsack DP over items and capacity
challenges.explanation: For each item, either skip it or take it: dp[w] = max(dp[w], dp[w − weight] + value). Iterate w downward so each item is used once.
